Manx: O ! Cre ta Dooinney ?
English: Oh! What is Man?

Manx: O ! cre ta dooinney, quoi dys neem’s soylagh eh ?
English: Oh! what is Man, to whom shall I compare him?

Manx: Ny cre ta towshan glaie slane eash e vea ?
English: Or what is a summary of his whole life?

Manx: Te myr yn blaa aalyn sy voghery,
English: He is like a beautiful flower in the morning,

Manx: Eisht giarit sheese as fiogit roish yn oie.
English: Then cut down and shrivelled up before the night.

Manx: Ta paart dy sleih ta kinjagh ayns imnea,
English: Some people are always in a state of anxiety,

Manx: Er eer fairdail kinjagh nyn aigney ta ;
English: There minds are always upon vanity ;

Manx: Myr nagh beagh ad dy bragh yn seihll aggail ;
English: As though they would never leave the world ;

Manx: Ny smooinaght er quoi t'oc ny [nyn] gooyl ny quaail,
English: Or think about who is behind them or towards (them),

Manx: My nee shiu ronsagh magh trooid sushtal Yee,
English: If you will seach through God’s gospel,

Manx: Ayns shen cha vow shiu moylley mooar erbee :
English: You will not find any great praise there :

Manx: Cour lheid y sleih ta son yn seihll shoh paa,
English: For such people who are thirsty for this world;

Manx: Nagh vel chur geill dy cosney maynrys braa.
English: Not paying attention to achieving eternal happiness.

Manx: T’ad girree moghrey gyn smooinaght er y Chiarn,
English: They rise early without a thought about a the Lord,

Manx: Dy re e phooar ta’r coadey ad ayns dagh Ayrn ;
English: That it is his power that has protected them in every part;

Manx: Throoid whilleen gaue t’ad fakin myr t’ad shooyl.
English: Through so many dangers they see as they walk,

Manx: As throoid danjeyr nagh vaik ad lesh nyn sooill
English: And through danger they did not see with their eyes

Manx: Cha vel ad croymmey sheese cur ooashley da,
English: They do not bend down worshipping him,

Manx: Ny er E ennym graihagh wheesh gimraa ;
English: Or so much as mention his loving name,

Manx: Dy cur da booise son slaynt, as son dagh nhee,
English: To thank him for health, and for everything,

Manx: Son coadey ad ayns gaueyn mooar yn oie.
English: For pretecting them in the great dangers of the night.

Manx: Ga ta shiu clashtyn kinjagh laa lurg laa,
English: Although you hear constantly day after day,

Manx: Jeh slatt y Chiarn er feiy ny cruinney ta ;
English: Of the rod of the Lord throughout the world ;

Manx: Paart ta slayntoil yn tra t’ad goll dy lhie,
English: Some who are fine (healthy) when they go to bed,

Manx: Fosley nyn sooillyn ayns seihll dy spyrrydyn sthie ?
English: Opening their eyes in a world of inner spirits ?

Manx: Paart ta gholl magh er gys nyn obbyr laa,
English: Some who go on out to their daytime work,

Manx: Nagh vel dy bragh reesh gys nyn dhieyn chyndaa.
English: Who never return again to their homes.

Manx: Ta’n baase doaltattym geamagh ad ersooyl,
English: Sudden death calls them away,

Manx: Eisht, cooid yn seihll shegin daue fagail ny gooyl.
English: Then, worldy goods they must leave behind

Manx: Shoh eisht, my chaarjyn, cronney shenn as aeg.
English: This then, my friends, is the fate of old and young.

Manx: Cha leah’s ta’n chaghter cheet dy gheddyn ad,
English: As soon as the messenger comes to get them,

Manx: Cha leah’s te geam shegin dooin dy bean [beayn] goll roin,
English: As soon as he calls we must go for ever,

Manx: As livrey sheese nyn girp gys ooir as joan.
English: And deliver up our bodies to the earth and dust.

Manx: Quoi eisht veagh moyrnagh as  mooarane cooid sy theihll,
English: Who then would be proud with a lot of worldly goods,

Manx: Tra shegin dooin eh ayns traa cha giare aagail ?
English: When we must in leave it in sucha short time?

Manx: Ooilley yn seihll dy yinnin cosney eh,
English: All the world, if we could gain it,

Manx: Cha vod eh choyrt un laa dys eash my vea.
English: It could not add one day to the length of my life.

Manx: Paart ayns yn caggey ta nyn mioys coayll
English: Some in war, their lives lose,

Manx: Paart er yn aarkey gys yn dinnid gholl,
English: Some on the ocean go to the deep,

Manx: As liorish aile paart elley er coyrt mow ;
English: And by fire some others are destroyed ;

Manx: Kys lhisagh shin ta’n mayrn goaill tastey jiu.
English: How ought we who are left take note today?

Manx: Ta dagh unnane oc shoh dooin son sampleyr,
English: Each one of them are here an example for us,

Manx: Greinnaghey shin dy hooyl sy cassan cair,
English: Urging us to walk in the righteous path,

Manx: Yn raad mooar lhean ta leeideil gys yn vaase,
English: The great wide road leads to death,

Manx: Yn cassan coon leeideil gys bea as grayse.
English: The righteous path leads to life and grace.

Manx: Bannit ta’n sleih nee coyrle y ghoaill sy traa,
English: Blessed are the people who will take advice in time,

Manx: Nee shickyr yannoo jeh nyn eiraght braa,
English: Who make secure their eternal inheritance,

Manx: Nee Yeesey ghraihagh ghoaill ad huggey hene
English: Who Jesus will lovingly take to himself,

Manx: Marish dy reill ayns seihllyn er nyn skin.
English: With him to rule in worlds above us.

Manx: Yeesey, nyn garrey kinjagh crankal ta,
English: Jesus, our friend is constatly knocking,

Manx: Geamagh dooin ooilley “D’osley yn dorrys da.”
English: Calling to us all “To open the door to him.”

Manx: Naightyn gloyroil diu ta jeh peccah skee,
English: Glorious new for you who are tired of sin,

Manx: Dy vel yn Chiarn meriu reih shibber ee.
English: That the Lord is with you choosing a supper to eat.

Manx: Eisht! dagh unnane ver enn er e corraa,
English: Then! each one will recognise his voice,

Manx: Nee girree seose as fosley’n dorrys da.
English: Will rise up and open the door for him.

Manx: Nee nyn Saualtagh maroo shoh cheet stiagh,
English: Our saviour will come in with them,

Manx: Eiyree eh’n noid yn Drogh-spyrrid moyrnagh magh.
English: He will drive the enemy, the proud devil, out.

Manx: Eisht Ree mooar Niau nee toshiaght ghoaill dy reill
English: Then the great King of Heaven will begin to rule

Manx: Ayns dagh persoon nee peccaghyn hreigeil,
English: In every person sins will abandon,

Manx: Lheeidee eh ad ayns obbyryn messoill,
English: He will lead them in fruitful works,

Manx: As coamrey ad lesh coamraghyn gloyroil.
English: And clothe them with glorious clothing.

Manx: She shoh nyn garrey, kinjagh jin gimraa,
English: This is our friend, always mentioning us,

Manx: Kionefenish Ayr lesh accan jeean daghlaa ;
English: In the presence of Father with earnest petition each day ;

Manx: Graa: O, my Ayr jean m’accan jeean ansoor,
English: Saying: O, my Father answer my earnest petition,

Manx: Ass lieh sheelnaue ta beaghey er yn ooir.
English: On behalf of humanity that lives on the Earth.

Manx: Shoh oyr dy wooise dooinyn as dagh unnane,
English: This is reason of thanks for us and every one,

Manx: Dy inshlagh sheese nyn greeaghyn gys yn Chiarn,
English: To humble our hearts to the Lord,

Manx: Yn nah persoon ta shassoo ayns quayl niau,
English: The second person who stands in heaven’s court,

Manx: Ren deayrtey uill dy kionnaghey sheelnaue.
English: Who shed his blood to purchase humanity.

Manx: Va dooinney crooit lesh aigney, glen, as free,
English: Man was created with will, pure, and free,

Manx: As fegooish dooyt ayns eer cochaslys Yee ;
English: And without doubt in the very image of God ;

Manx: Eisht ren y noid y vaynrys roostey voue,
English: Then the enemy robbed the happiness from them,

Manx: Ass gharey Eden chelleeragh v’ad jeight mooie.
English: Out of Eden, straight away, they were shut out.

Manx: Ga va’d gyn logh tra va’d sy gharey sthie,
English: Though they were without sin when they were inside the garden,

Manx: Cha moo va oc tushtey, jeh mie as sie,
English: As soon as they had intelligence, of good and evil,

Manx: Cha leah as ren ad jeh yn villey ghee,
English: As soon as ate of the tree,

Manx: Chelleeragh hoig ad dy vrish ad sarey Yee.
English: The immediately realised that they broke God’s command.

Manx: Eisht ooilley’n chroo chelleeragh gow caghlaa,
English: Then all of creation immediately changed,

Manx: Eer maase y vaghragh, marish yeeanlee ’n aer ;
English: Even the cattle of the field, as well as the birds of the sky ;

Manx: Roish shoh v’ad ooilley cooidjagh beaghey ayns graih,
English: Before this they were all together living in love,

Manx: Agh nish t’ad ooilley ayns olkys noi ry hoi.
English: But now they are all in evil against eachother.

Manx: Adam va mâroo coyrt my ner dagh nhee,
English: Adam was with them observing everything,

Manx: Dyn dooyt, my chaarjyn, atchim ayns e chree.
English: No doubt, my friends, terror in his heart.

Manx: Booishal dagh olk, gys mie reesht y hyndaa,
English: Wishing each evil, to turn again to good,

Manx: Agh va’n tra harrish ve nish ro anmagh daa.
English: But the time was over, it was now too late for it.

Manx: As ga dy ren eh brasnagh e er chroo,
English: And although he stirred his creator,

Manx: As nagh ren tannaghtyn dy reayl e ghoo,
English: And did not continue to keep his word,

Manx: Foast loayr Jee rish lesh fockleyn lane dy graih,
English: Still God spoke to him with words full of love,

Manx: Ginsh da yn saase dy cosney’n eiraght thie.
English: Telling him the method to get his inheritance home.

Manx: She ayns yn astyr ta’n Scriptyr Bannit graa,
English: It is in the afternoon, the Blessed Scripture says,

Manx: Ren Jee cheet neose as loayrt lesh ard corraa,
English: That God came down and spoke with a loud voice,

Manx: “Adam, my vac ! tar as jean shassoo roym ;
English: “Adam, my son! come and stand begofe me ;

Manx: Cre'n fa t’ou shirrey d' ollagh[1] d’eddin voym ?”
English: Why are you trying, hid your face from me?”
Notes: [1] dy ’ollagh] ‘to hide’, original gives [dollee] ‘hid’ which is evidently a typo.

Manx: Adam er creau s’coan abyl cur ansoor,
English: Adam shaking, hardly able to answer,

Manx: Dy heet kionefenish yn ooilley niartal pooar,
English: At coming into the presence of the almighty power,

Manx: Foast beign da cheet as shoh myr ren eh graa :
English: Still he had to come and this is how he spoke:

Manx: “Roie me er chea tra cheeayl me dy corraa.”
English: “I ran away when I heard your voice.”

Manx: “Cre’n oyr” dooyrt Jee: “T’ou shirrey voym scapail ?
English: “Why” said God: “You’re trying to escape from me?

Manx: Nagh bollogh oo lesh boggey cheet my whail,
English: Did you not used to come to meet me with joy?

Manx: Jeeagh d’eddin dow, shass magh as soilshee eh.
English: Show me your face, stand out and illuminate it.

Manx: Cre’n oyr t’ou voish d’er chroo nish roie er chea?”
English: Why are you, from your creator, now running away?”

Manx: Eisht dansoor Adam as hoilshee eh y chooish :
English: Then Ada answered and he explained the matter :

Manx: “Roie me er chea er son dy row mee rooisht,
English: “I ran away because I was naked,

Manx: She shoh va’n oyr ta nearey ayns my chree,
English: This is why there was shame in my heart,

Manx: Dy heet kionefenish yn ooilley niartial Jee.”
English: To come into the presence of the almighty God.”

Manx: “Quoi dinsh dhyt d’ell oo rooisht?" eisht dooyrt y Chiarn.
English: “Who told you that you were naked?” then the Lord said

Manx: “Vel oo er n’ee jeh mess yn villey shen
English: “Have oo eaten of the fruit of that tree?

Manx: V’ayns mean yn gharey dinsh mee dhyt ro laue
English: That was in the middle of garden the I told you beforehand

Manx: Va tayrn lesh baase ort hene as slane sheel naue?”
English: Was drawing death upon you and the whole of humanity?”

Manx: Eisht dansoor Adam as dooyrt eh rish er chroo:
English: Then Adam answered and he said to his creator:

Manx: “Te kindagh rish yn ven shen hug oo dow ;
English: “It is because of that woman he gave to me ;

Manx: Ghow ish jeh roym as ren ee miollagh mee,
English: She went off before me and she tempted me,

Manx: Dy ee jeh’n mess gyn smooinaght olk erbee.”
English: To eat of the fruit without thinking anything bad.”

Manx: Eisht dooyrt yn Chiarn : “Cre’n olk shoh ta jeant ayd,
English: Then the Lord said : “What is this evil that you have done,

Manx: Cre’n fa ren uss dy heshey cur jeh’n raad ?
English: Why did you put your partner off the road ?

Manx: Uss lhisagh veih goaill slane sampleyr dy veh,
English: You, who should from him take a full example of being,

Manx: Er chur da mess dy cur er shaghryn eh.”
English: Have given him fruit to send him astray.”

Manx: Chelleeragh Eve ren playnt er yn ardnieu :
English: Straightaway, Eve complained about the snake :

Manx: “Dy ren eh miolagh ayns yn raad oc jiu ;
English: “That he tempted in their way today :

Manx: Son dooyrt eh rym eh nee jeh’n mess shoh ghee,
English: For he said to me he who will eat of this fruit,

Manx: Chelleeragh bee eh chreeney goll rish Jee.”
English: He will immediately be wise like God.”

Manx: Eisht hug yn Chiarn fo mollaght yn ardnieu,
English: Then the Lord cursed the snake,

Manx: As dooyrt Eh : “Rish she er dty volg nee oo snaue;
English: And He said : “You will crawl on your stomach;

Manx: As son nagh bee ayds oyr nish dy voasteill,
English: And because you will not have reason to boast,

Manx: Er skyn sluight Eve dy bragh cha jean oo reill.
English: Above Eve’s offspring you will never rule.

Manx: “As uss y ven, nish son dy hass oo da,
English: “And you woman, now because you stood for him,

Manx: T’ou er dayrn ort hene trimshey son dy braa ;
English: You have drawn upon yourself sadness for ever;

Manx: She ayns angaish nee oo cloan cur son y theihll,
English: In anguish you will bring forth children into the world,

Manx: Dty heshey hene myrgheddin harryds reill.”
English: Your own partner also ruling over you.”

Manx: Eisht ren yn Chiarn rish Adam loayrt dy plain :
English: Then to the Lord to Adam spoke plainly :

Manx: “Er son dy ren oo geaishtagh rish e[2] ven,
English: “Because you listened to your wife,

Manx: T’ou er dayrn mollaght trome or ooilley’n ooir,
English: You have drawn a heavy curse upon all the earth,

Manx: Eer dty heeloghe hene myrgheddin dagh cretoor.
English: Even your own generation as well as every creature.

Manx: “Drinenyn as dressyn nee dy palchey gaase;
English: “Thorns and brambles will grow plentifully;

Manx: Nee oo dt’arran gee lesh ollish trome dty[3] vaaish,
English: You will eat your bread the with heavy sweat of your brow,

Manx: Shoh vees dty currym kinjagh laa lurg laa,
English: This will be your duty always, day after day,

Manx: Er derry nee oo reesht dys ooir chyndaa.”
English: Until you will return to earth.

Manx: Adam as Eve ny neesht hie er chyndaa,
English: Adam and Eve both were turned,

Manx: Ass garey Eden jeight er son dy braa,
English: Out of the Garden of Eden shut, for ever,

Manx: Lesh chreeaghyn brish as sooillyn lane dy yeir,
English: With broken hearts and eyes full of tears,

Manx: Beign daue nyn ghooyl cur rish yn eiraght cair.
English: They had to put the righteous inheritance behind them.

Manx: Eisht cherubim voish chooyrtyn sollys niau,
English: Then cherubim from the bright courts of heaven,

Manx: Ren Jee coyrt neose dy insh nyn gurrym daue,
English: That God sent down to tell their duties to them,

Manx: Lesh cliwe ailagh fendeil yn garey voue[4],
English: With fiery sword defended the garden from them,

Manx: Lhiettall yn raad lheideil gys billey yn vea.
English: Blocking the way leading to the tree of life.

Manx: Foast cha ren Jee Adam as Eve hreigeil,
English: Still God did not abandon Adam and Eve,

Manx: Lesh focklyn graihagh ren eh roo pleadeil;
English: With loving words he pleaded to them;

Manx: Chooatyn dy chraitnyn ren eh yannoo daue,
English: Coats of skins he made for them,

Manx: Dy reayll veih’n feayraght Ayr as moir sheelnaue.
English: To keep the Father and mother of humanity from the cold.

Manx: Nish gloyr as booise dy bragh gys Chreest nyn Jiarn,
English: Now eternal glory and thanks to Christ our Lord,

Manx: Ren gymmyrk lesh yn dooinney as yn ven ;
English: Who put up with the man and the woman ;

Manx: Nagh ren eh ad ayns E ymmoose cur mow,
English: Who he did not in his fury destroy,

Manx: Agh yiall eh daue eiraght ayns reeriaght niau.
English: Rather he promised them an inheritance in the kingdom of heaven

Manx: Ard ooashley feen[5] dy row da Jee dy braa,
English: Majesty may there be to God evermore,
Notes: [5] feen] meaning unlcear here, so left untranslated.

Manx: Ta ayns e vyghin coadey shin dagh laa,
English: Who in his mercy pretects us each day,

Manx: Ren cur E vac ghraysoil dy hurranse baase
English: Who gaves his graceful son to suffer death

Manx: Da peccee hreih dy cosney bea as grayse.
English: For miserable sinners to gain life and grace.
